headline: High-risk shared-file and action pipeline: MinerU can feed untrusted document content into Plandex, which has filesystem write and shell/network authority.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes MCP/API surfaces, so its extracted text can be passed into Plandex. Plandex reads files and supports review-then-apply workflows, making prompt injection plausible if document content is treated as instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into Plandex prompts or plans without sanitization
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled for content derived from MinerU
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Insert a manual review step for all MinerU-derived text
Strip instructions and code blocks from extracted documents
Use a fixed prompt template that labels MinerU output as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between MinerU and Plandex

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU processes sensitive document classes such as PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX. Plandex has broad network egress and can read project files, so if MinerU outputs are placed in the shared workspace, document contents may flow into a third-party model provider. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary that would make this impossible.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are stored in the same project directory Plandex reads
IF Plandex sends those files or prompts to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate directory
Exclude sensitive documents from Plandex inputs
Use a local-only model backend for Plandex
Review Plandex file inclusion before each run
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-only on filesystem but can use MCP and concurrent inference; Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same project directory, Plandex can overwrite or commit artifacts derived from MinerU outputs, creating a dangerous write conflict in default developer workflows.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working directory
IF Plandex applies changes while MinerU is still producing outputs
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Disable Plandex auto-apply
Serialize runs so MinerU finishes before Plandex edits
Use git branches for Plandex changes
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted facts from documents, and Plandex is a planner that can turn file contents into code or edits. If Plandex treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect plans or commits. The profiles do not show a verification gate strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF Plandex uses MinerU extraction as direct input to planning
IF no human or automated verification checks the extracted facts
mitigations: Require human review of extracted facts before planning
Cross-check key fields against the source document
Limit MinerU output to quoted spans with page references
Keep Plandex in review-only mode until verification passes
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU handles document classes that may include regulated content, while Plandex explicitly sends data to a model provider and handles API keys. If regulated documents are routed from MinerU into Plandex, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible rather than blocked.
conditions: IF regulated documents from MinerU are forwarded into Plandex
IF the model provider or Plandex backend retains prompts beyond policy
mitigations: Do not route regulated documents into Plandex
Use a local/self-hosted Plandex backend
Confirm retention settings before processing sensitive files
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency map
